newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworkers unions, employers sign pay deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworkers unions, employers sign pay deal.

text.p: Italian engineering and metalworkers unions and employers signed a deal on contracts on Tuesday, ending a bitter and protracted dispute in the key industrial sector, Labour Minister Tiziano Treu said.
"The contract has been signed," Treu said as both sides gathered at the ministry to sign the agreement. Journalists witnessed the signing.
"It was a difficult contract that couldn't satisfy everyone completely. But I am satisfied because just 24 hours ago, there were still doubts," Treu said.

The FIM, FIOM and UILM unions represent 1.7 million workers in a sector accounting for 40 percent of Italian industrial output. They and employers' group Federmeccanica had been at loggerheads since previous two-year contracts ran out last June.
"This is a deal which leaves everyone both satisfied and dissatisfied," Federmeccanica director-general Michele Figurati said. "Let's hope we can do better next time."

The government-brokered deal is based on a 30-month contract and a one-off payment of 512,000 lire ($316) paid in two instalments to cover the first six months, followed by graduated monthly wage increases totalling 200,000 lire ($124) during the rest of the contract.
